variant_id=CYBB-p.His101Arg gene=CYBB accession=P04839 position=101 reference=H alternate=R

Task: PLAN. Read hypotheses H1-H3 and evidence E1-E20 from the record. Write at least 2 test candidates with expected learning, feasibility and cost, within the remaining budget (check get_budget_status). Write one plan that chooses a single test and gives a reason for each rejected one. Then hand off to the orchestrator.

output: {"objective":"Find the molecular mechanism that best explains the loss of function of CYBB-p.His101Arg (CYBB, UniProt P04839) and test it with one targeted computational test.","subject":{"gene":"CYBB","variant_id":"CYBB-p.His101Arg","accession":"P04839","position":101,"reference_residue":"H","alternate_residue":"R","protein_change":"p.His101Arg"},"events":36,"current_favourite":"H1","gaps":[{"id":"G1","by":"literature","statement":"None of the retrieved abstracts or titles mention His101 or the substitution H101R in CYBB/gp91phox, so the literature does not establish the residue's role in heme coordination, folding, or electron transfer."},{"id":"G2","by":"literature","statement":"No retrieved paper reports expression, maturation, heme incorporation, or superoxide production for a CYBB variant with an Arg substitution at position 101."},{"id":"G3","by":"knowledge_graph","statement":"No experimental structure in the PDB records the mutated residue: of the 5 entries observing residue 101, 0 have it mutated."},{"id":"G4","by":"knowledge_graph","statement":"Functional assays covering residue 101 of P04839: 0 reported."},{"id":"G5","by":"knowledge_graph","statement":"IntAct rows for P04839 (SPOP, CYBC1, FBXW7) do not map their interaction surfaces to residues, so no interaction is tied to residue 101."}],"hypotheses":[{"id":"H1","mechanism_class":"ligand_binding","starting_rank":1,"statement":"His101 is the axial heme b ligand of gp91phox (CYBB). Replacing it with Arg removes the imidazole that coordinates the heme iron, so the heme cannot be held in the cytochrome b558 core and electron transfer from FAD to O2 fails.","supports":["E3","E15","E17","E18","E1","E8","E10","E20"],"would_refute":"The His101 side chain in the heme-bound cryo-EM structures (8WEJ, 8X2L, 7U8G) is not within coordination distance (about 2.5 Å) of the heme iron, or His101 is shown to be a non-coordinating residue. Equally, an Arg placed at 101 in a model that keeps the heme iron in place with a plausible ligand at the Arg position would weaken this hypothesis.","latest_verdict":"untested","label":"agent-generated hypothesis"},{"id":"H2","mechanism_class":"stability_folding","starting_rank":2,"statement":"His101 sits in the transmembrane helix (residues 96-130) of gp91phox. Inserting a charged Arg into the membrane-embedded helix destabilises the four-helix cytochrome b558 fold, so the protein misfolds, is degraded, and fails to mature with p22phox.","supports":["E4","E8","E10","E11","E13","E12","E1"],"would_refute":"A stability calculation or MD run of the H101R model shows no significant destabilisation (for example ddG under about 1 kcal/mol, with the Arg side chain placed to avoid burial of charge). Or His101 is shown to be solvent-exposed and outside the membrane in the resolved structures, so it does not contribute to the helix packing.","latest_verdict":"untested","label":"agent-generated hypothesis"},{"id":"H3","mechanism_class":"protein_interaction","starting_rank":3,"statement":"His101 is at the gp91phox–p22phox heterodimer interface in the transmembrane region. The His-to-Arg change alters that contact, so p22phox cannot stabilise gp91phox, and the flavocytochrome b558 heterodimer does not form.","supports":["E5","E12","E7","E9"],"would_refute":"In the resolved NOX2–p22phox structures (8WEJ, 7U8G), no atom of His101 lies within about 4–5 Å of any p22phox residue, and the buried surface of the p22phox interface does not include residue 101.","latest_verdict":"untested","label":"agent-generated hypothesis"}],"tests":[],"plans":[],"results":[],"decisions":[],"notes":[]}
